sanskrit: janaka uvāca kāni karmāṇi dharmyāṇi loke 'smin dvijasattama na hiṃsantīha bhūtāni kriyamāṇāni sarvadā
english: Janaka said: O best of the twice-born, which deeds are in keeping with dharma, such that, when performed in this world, they never bring harm to living beings at any time?

sanskrit: parāśara uvāca śṛṇu me 'tra mahārāja yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi yāni karmāṇy ahiṃsrāṇi naraṃ trāyanti sarvadā
english: Parāśara said: Hear from me, O great king, the answer to what you ask of me — those deeds free of harm, which always deliver a man to safety.

sanskrit: saṃnyasyāgnīn upāsīnāḥ paśyanti vigatajvarāḥ naiḥśreyasaṃ dharmapathaṃ samāruhya yathākramam
english: Having laid aside the sacred fires and sitting in devotion, freed of feverish care, they behold — step by step ascending the dharma-path that leads to the highest good.

sanskrit: praśritā vinayopetā damanityāḥ susaṃśitāḥ prayānti sthānam ajaraṃ sarvakarmavivarjitāḥ
english: Humble, endowed with discipline, ever devoted to self-restraint and well-tempered, they go forth to the ageless abode, having renounced all works.

sanskrit: sarve varṇā dharmakāryāṇi samyak; kṛtvā rājan satyavākyāni coktvā tyaktvādharmaṃ dāruṇaṃ jīvaloke; yānti svargaṃ nātra kāryo vicāraḥ
english: All the varṇas, O king, having rightly performed the works of dharma and spoken words of truth, having cast off cruel unrighteousness while in the world of the living, attain to heaven — of this there can be no doubt.

sanskrit: parāśara uvāca pitā sakhāyo guravaḥ striyaś ca; na nirguṇā nāma bhavanti loke ananyabhaktāḥ priyavādinaś ca; hitāś ca vaśyāś ca tathaiva rājan
english: Parāśara said: A father, friends, elders, and wives are never, in this world, devoid of worth, O king — they are single-hearted in devotion, kindly in speech, well-wishing, and obedient alike.

sanskrit: pitā paraṃ daivataṃ mānavānāṃ; mātur viśiṣṭaṃ pitaraṃ vadanti jñānasya lābhaṃ paramaṃ vadanti; jitendriyārthāḥ param āpnuvanti
english: The father is the supreme deity of men; greater even than the mother do they call the father. They declare the gaining of knowledge to be the highest gain, and those who have conquered the objects of the senses attain the supreme.

sanskrit: raṇājire yatra śarāgnisaṃstare; nṛpātmajo ghātam avāpya dahyate prayāti lokān amaraiḥ sudurlabhān; niṣevate svargaphalaṃ yathāsukham
english: On the battlefield, where the strewn bed is the fire of arrows, the prince who meets his slaying is consumed there; he passes to worlds scarce won even by the immortals, and enjoys the fruit of heaven at his ease.

sanskrit: śrāntaṃ bhītaṃ bhraṣṭaśastraṃ rudantaṃ; parāṅmukhaṃ paribarhaiś ca hīnam anudyataṃ rogiṇaṃ yācamānaṃ; na vai hiṃsyād bālavṛddhau ca rājan
english: The weary man, the frightened, the one whose weapon has fallen, the weeping, the one who has turned his back, the one stripped of attendants, the unresisting, the sick, the suppliant — these one must not strike, O king, nor the child nor the aged.

sanskrit: paribarhaiḥ susaṃpannam udyataṃ tulyatāṃ gatam atikrameta nṛpatiḥ saṃgrāme kṣatriyātmajam
english: Only one well-furnished with attendants, ready for combat, and come to an equal footing — such a son of the kṣatriyas may the king assail in battle.

sanskrit: tulyād iha vadhaḥ śreyān viśiṣṭāc ceti niścayaḥ nihīnāt kātarāc caiva nṛpāṇāṃ garhito vadhaḥ
english: Death at the hands of an equal, or of a superior, is the better lot — such is the settled view; but the slaying of the lowly and the timid is, for kings, a blameworthy deed.

sanskrit: pāpāt pāpasamācārān nihīnāc ca narādhipa pāpa eva vadhaḥ prokto narakāyeti niścayaḥ
english: To slay one who is wicked, of wicked conduct, and base, O lord of men, is itself declared a sin that leads to hell — so it is determined.

sanskrit: na kaś cit trāti vai rājan diṣṭāntavaśam āgatam sāvaśeṣāyuṣaṃ cāpi kaś cid evāpakarṣati
english: No one, O king, can save the man who has come under the power of his appointed end; yet one whose span of life still has a remainder, someone may indeed drag back from death.

sanskrit: snigdhaiś ca kriyamāṇāni karmāṇīha nivartayet hiṃsātmakāni karmāṇi nāyur icchet parāyuṣā
english: Deeds being done by those who are dear should here be turned away from harm; one should not, by deeds whose nature is violence, seek long life at the cost of another's life.

sanskrit: gṛhasthānāṃ tu sarveṣāṃ vināśam abhikāṅkṣatām nidhanaṃ śobhanaṃ tāta pulineṣu kriyāvatām
english: But for all householders who long for the dissolution of self, the death is a fair one, dear son, when, performing their rites, they die upon the sandbanks of holy rivers.

sanskrit: āyuṣi kṣayam āpanne pañcatvam upagacchati nākāraṇāt tad bhavati kāraṇair upapāditam
english: When one's span comes to its wasting, he attains dissolution into the five elements; this does not happen without cause — it is brought about by causes.

sanskrit: tathā śarīraṃ bhavati dehād yenopapāditam adhvānaṃ gatakaś cāyaṃ prāptaś cāyaṃ gṛhād gṛham
english: Thus a body comes to be, brought into being from a former body; this one has gone along the road, and this one has passed from house to house.

sanskrit: dvitīyaṃ kāraṇaṃ tatra nānyat kiṃ cana vidyate tad dehaṃ dehināṃ yuktaṃ mokṣabhūteṣu vartate
english: There is no second cause to be found in this, none other whatsoever; that body, joined to the embodied, abides among the things subject to release.

sanskrit: sirāsnāyvasthisaṃghātaṃ bībhatsāmedhyasaṃkulam bhūtānām indriyāṇāṃ ca guṇānāṃ ca samāgamam
english: A frame of veins, sinews, and bones, crowded with what is loathsome and impure, a meeting-place of the elements, the senses, and the qualities —

sanskrit: tvagantaṃ deham ity āhur vidvāṃso 'dhyātmacintakāḥ guṇair api parikṣīṇaṃ śarīraṃ martyatāṃ gatam
english: this, bounded by the skin, the learned who ponder the inner Self call the body; the body, worn away even of its qualities, has come to its mortal end.

sanskrit: śarīriṇā parityaktaṃ niśceṣṭaṃ gatacetanam bhūtaiḥ prakṛtim āpannais tato bhūmau nimajjati
english: Abandoned by the embodied Self, motionless and devoid of consciousness, with its elements returned to their native source, it then sinks down into the earth.

sanskrit: bhāvitaṃ karmayogena jāyate tatra tatra ha idaṃ śarīraṃ vaideha mriyate yatra tatra ha tatsvabhāvo 'paro dṛṣṭo visargaḥ karmaṇas tathā
english: Shaped by the working of past deeds, it is born here and there; this body, O prince of Videha, dies here and there; another such nature is seen, and likewise the casting-off that is the fruit of action.

sanskrit: na jāyate tu nṛpate kaṃ cit kālam ayaṃ punaḥ paribhramati bhūtātmā dyām ivāmbudharo mahān
english: Yet for a certain time, O king, this elemental self is not born again; it wanders about, like a great rain-cloud across the sky.

sanskrit: sa punar jāyate rājan prāpyehāyatanaṃ nṛpa manasaḥ paramo hy ātmā indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ manaḥ
english: Then he is born again, O king, having gained here an abode; for the Self is higher than the mind, and the mind is higher than the senses.

sanskrit: dvividhānāṃ ca bhūtānāṃ jaṅgamāḥ paramā nṛpa jaṅgamānām api tathā dvipadāḥ paramā matāḥ dvipadānām api tathā dvijā vai paramāḥ smṛtāḥ
english: Of beings, which are of two kinds, the moving are held supreme, O king; among the moving, the two-footed are deemed supreme; and among the two-footed, the twice-born are remembered as supreme.

sanskrit: dvijānām api rājendra prajñāvantaḥ parā matāḥ prājñānām ātmasaṃbuddhāḥ saṃbuddhānām amāninaḥ
english: Among the twice-born too, O lord of kings, the wise are deemed supreme; among the wise, those awakened to the Self; and among the awakened, those free of pride.

sanskrit: jātam anveti maraṇaṃ nṛṇām iti viniścayaḥ antavanti hi karmāṇi sevante guṇataḥ prajāḥ
english: Death follows close upon the born — this is the settled truth for men; for deeds have their end, and the creatures pursue them according to their qualities.

sanskrit: āpanne tūttarāṃ kāṣṭhāṃ sūrye yo nidhanaṃ vrajet nakṣatre ca muhūrte ca puṇye rājan sa puṇyakṛt
english: When the sun has reached its northern course, he who comes to his death under an auspicious constellation and at an auspicious hour, O king, is a doer of merit.

sanskrit: ayojayitvā kleśena janaṃ plāvya ca duṣkṛtam mṛtyunāprākṛteneha karma kṛtvātmaśaktitaḥ
english: Without burdening folk with affliction, and having washed away his ill deeds, he dies here by a death that is not common, having performed his works according to his own power.

sanskrit: viṣam udbandhanaṃ dāho dasyuhastāt tathā vadhaḥ daṃṣṭribhyaś ca paśubhyaś ca prākṛto vadha ucyate
english: Poison, hanging, burning, slaying at the hand of robbers, and death by fanged beasts and by cattle — such a death is called a common one.

sanskrit: na caibhiḥ puṇyakarmāṇo yujyante nābhisaṃdhijaiḥ evaṃvidhaiś ca bahubhir aparaiḥ prākṛtair api
english: And the doers of meritorious deeds are not joined to these, nor to such as spring from violent intent, nor to many others of like common sort.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ hitvā pratiṣṭhante prāṇāḥ puṇyakṛtāṃ nṛpa madhyato madhyapuṇyānām adho duṣkṛtakarmaṇām
english: Departing upward, the life-breaths take their station, O king, for the doers of merit; from the middle for those of middling merit; and downward for those whose deeds were ill.

sanskrit: ekaḥ śatrur na dvitīyo 'sti śatrur; ajñānatulyaḥ puruṣasya rājan yenāvṛtaḥ kurute saṃprayukto; ghorāṇi karmāṇi sudāruṇāni
english: There is but one foe, and no second foe, O king, equal to a man's own ignorance; veiled by it and set upon by it, he performs deeds dreadful and most cruel.

sanskrit: prabodhanārthaṃ śrutidharmayuktaṃ; vṛddhān upāsyaṃ ca bhaveta yasya prayatnasādhyo hi sa rājaputra; prajñāśareṇonmathitaḥ paraiti
english: He whose path to awakening lies through the dharma of sacred lore and the service of his elders — that foe, O prince, is to be conquered only by effort, and, churned away by the arrow of wisdom, it departs.

sanskrit: adhītya vedāṃs tapasā brahmacārī; yajñāñ śaktyā saṃnisṛjyeha pañca vanaṃ gacchet puruṣo dharmakāmaḥ; śreyaś citvā sthāpayitvā svavaṃśam
english: Having studied the Vedas in austerity as a celibate, and having here offered the five sacrifices as he is able, the man who desires dharma should go to the forest — having gathered up the higher good and established his lineage.

sanskrit: upabhogair api tyaktaṃ nātmānam avasādayet caṇḍālatve 'pi mānuṣyaṃ sarvathā tāta durlabham
english: Even when forsaken by every enjoyment, one should not let the self sink into despair; for human birth, even in the state of an outcaste, is in every way hard to win, dear son.

sanskrit: iyaṃ hi yoniḥ prathamā yāṃ prāpya jagatīpate ātmā vai śakyate trātuṃ karmabhiḥ śubhalakṣaṇaiḥ
english: For this is the foremost birth, O lord of the earth, on attaining which the self can be saved through deeds marked by auspiciousness.

sanskrit: kathaṃ na vipraṇaśyema yonito 'syā iti prabho kurvanti dharmaṃ manujāḥ śrutiprāmāṇyadarśanāt
english: "How may we not fall away from this birth?" — with this thought, O lord, men practise dharma, guided by their regard for the authority of sacred revelation.

sanskrit: yo durlabhataraṃ prāpya mānuṣyam iha vai naraḥ dharmāvamantā kāmātmā bhavet sa khalu vañcyate
english: The man who, having won this human state so very hard to attain, becomes a despiser of dharma and a slave to desire — he, surely, is deceived of his gain.

sanskrit: yas tu prītipurogeṇa cakṣuṣā tāta paśyati dīpopamāni bhūtāni yāvad arcir na naśyati
english: But he who, with an eye that goes before in loving-kindness, beholds living beings as lamps — for just so long as the flame does not die out, dear son —

sanskrit: sāntvenānupradānena priyavādena cāpy uta samaduḥkhasukho bhūtvā sa paratra mahīyate
english: by gentleness, by giving, and by kindly speech, becoming one to whom the sorrow and joy of others are as his own — he is exalted in the world beyond.

sanskrit: dānaṃ tyāgaḥ śobhanā mūrtir adbhyo; bhūyaḥ plāvyaṃ tapasā vai śarīram sarasvatīnaimiṣapuṣkareṣu; ye cāpy anye puṇyadeśāḥ pṛthivyām
english: Giving, renunciation, and a fair form arise from the waters; the body, moreover, is to be cleansed by austerity — at the Sarasvatī, at Naimiṣa, at Puṣkara, and at whatever other holy places there are upon the earth.

sanskrit: gṛheṣu yeṣām asavaḥ patanti; teṣām atho nirharaṇaṃ praśastam yānena vai prāpaṇaṃ ca śmaśāne; śaucena nūnaṃ vidhinā caiva dāhaḥ
english: For those whose life-breaths fall away within their homes, the bearing-out is then commended, and the conveying upon a bier to the cremation ground; and surely the burning, performed with purity and according to rule.

sanskrit: iṣṭiḥ puṣṭir yajanaṃ yājanaṃ ca; dānaṃ puṇyānāṃ karmaṇāṃ ca prayogaḥ śaktyā pitryaṃ yac ca kiṃ cit praśastaṃ; sarvāṇy ātmārthe mānavo yaḥ karoti
english: Sacrifice and nurture, offering for oneself and officiating for others, giving, and the practice of meritorious works; whatever rite to the fathers is commended, as one is able — all these a man performs for the sake of his own self.

sanskrit: dharmaśāstrāṇi vedāś ca ṣaḍaṅgāni narādhipa śreyaso 'rthe vidhīyante narasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ
english: The treatises on dharma, the Vedas, and the six auxiliary sciences, O lord of men, are ordained for the highest good of the man whose deeds are untainted.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evad vai sarvam ākhyātaṃ muninā sumahātmanā videharājāya purā śreyaso 'rthe narādhipa
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus indeed was all this declared of old by that sage of mighty soul to the king of the Videhas, for the sake of the highest good, O lord of men.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca punar eva tu papraccha janako mithilādhipaḥ parāśaraṃ mahātmānaṃ dharme paramaniścayam
english: Bhīṣma said: And once again Janaka, lord of Mithilā, questioned the great-souled Parāśara, supremely resolved in the knowledge of dharma.

sanskrit: kiṃ śreyaḥ kā gatir brahman kiṃ kṛtaṃ na vinaśyati kva gato na nivarteta tan me brūhi mahāmune
english: What is the highest good? What is the goal? O brāhmaṇa, what deed, once done, does not perish? Gone where, does one not return? Tell me this, O great sage.

sanskrit: parāśara uvāca asaṅgaḥ śreyaso mūlaṃ jñānaṃ jñānagatiḥ parā cīrṇaṃ tapo na praṇaśyed vāpaḥ kṣetre na naśyati
english: Parāśara said: Non-attachment is the root of the highest good; knowledge is the supreme goal of knowing. Austerity rightly practised does not perish, as water does not perish in a field.

sanskrit: chittvādharmamayaṃ pāśaṃ yadā dharme 'bhirajyate dattvābhayakṛtaṃ dānaṃ tadā siddhim avāpnuyāt
english: When, having cut the noose made of unrighteousness, one delights in dharma, and bestows the gift of fearlessness, then one would attain perfection.

sanskrit: yo dadāti sahasrāṇi gavām aśvaśatāni ca abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyas tad dānam ativartate
english: Though a man give thousands of cattle and hundreds of horses, the gift of fearlessness to all beings surpasses that giving.

sanskrit: vasan viṣayamadhye 'pi na vasaty eva buddhimān saṃvasaty eva durbuddhir asatsu viṣayeṣv api
english: The wise man, though he dwell amid the objects of sense, dwells not in them at all; while the dull-witted dwells fast in them, even among objects that are unreal.

sanskrit: nādharmaḥ śliṣyate prājñam āpaḥ puṣkaraparṇavat aprājñam adhikaṃ pāpaṃ śliṣyate jatu kāṣṭhavat
english: Unrighteousness clings not to the wise, as water clings not to the lotus-leaf; but to the unwise sin clings the more, as lac clings to wood.

sanskrit: nādharmaḥ kāraṇāpekṣī kartāram abhimuñcati kartā khalu yathākālaṃ tat sarvam abhipadyate na bhidyante kṛtātmāna ātmapratyayadarśinaḥ
english: Unrighteousness, awaiting its occasion, does not release the doer; the doer surely, in due time, meets with all of it. But those of perfected self, who behold the Self by direct conviction, are not broken by it.

sanskrit: buddhikarmendriyāṇāṃ hi pramatto yo na budhyate śubhāśubheṣu saktātmā prāpnoti sumahad bhayam
english: He who, heedless of his mind, his deeds, and his senses, does not awaken, and whose self is clinging to things good and evil, attains to a very great fear.

sanskrit: vītarāgo jitakrodhaḥ samyag bhavati yaḥ sadā viṣaye vartamāno 'pi na sa pāpena yujyate
english: He who is free of passion, has conquered anger, and is ever rightly poised — even while moving among the objects of sense, he is not joined to sin.

sanskrit: maryādāyāṃ dharmasetur nibaddho naiva sīdati puṣṭasrota ivāyattaḥ sphīto bhavati saṃcayaḥ
english: The dyke of dharma, bound firmly within its bounds, never gives way; and held in check like a swelling current, the store of merit grows abundant.

sanskrit: yathā bhānugataṃ tejo maṇiḥ śuddhaḥ samādhinā ādatte rājaśārdūla tathā yogaḥ pravartate
english: As a pure gem takes up, by its fixed disposition, the brilliance that comes from the sun, O tiger among kings, so does yoga come into operation.

sanskrit: yathā tilānām iha puṣpasaṃśrayāt; pṛthak pṛthag yāti guṇo 'tisaumyatām tathā narāṇāṃ bhuvi bhāvitātmanāṃ; yathāśrayaṃ sattvaguṇaḥ pravartate
english: As the essence of sesame seeds, from their resort to flowers, passes severally into a surpassing sweetness, so among men upon the earth whose selves are refined, the quality of goodness unfolds according to that on which it rests.

sanskrit: jahāti dārān ihate na saṃpadaḥ; sadaśvayānaṃ vividhāś ca yāḥ kriyāḥ triviṣṭape jātamatir yadā naras; tadāsya buddhir viṣayeṣu bhidyate
english: He forsakes his wife, and longs no more for fortunes, for fine horses and chariots and the manifold rites; when a man's mind is born toward the heaven of the gods, then his understanding parts from the objects of sense.

sanskrit: prasaktabuddhir viṣayeṣu yo naro; yo budhyate hy ātmahitaṃ kadā ca na sa sarvabhāvānugatena cetasā; nṛpāmiṣeṇeva jhaṣo vikṛṣyate
english: The man whose understanding is fastened upon the objects of sense, who never once awakens to his own true welfare — with a mind running after every passing state, he is dragged off like a fish by the bait, O king.

sanskrit: saṃghātavān martyalokaḥ parasparam apāśritaḥ kadalīgarbhaniḥsāro naur ivāpsu nimajjati
english: The world of mortals is a thing held together, each leaning upon the other, hollow at the core like the trunk of a plantain; it sinks down like a boat upon the waters.

sanskrit: na dharmakālaḥ puruṣasya niścito; na cāpi mṛtyuḥ puruṣaṃ pratīkṣate kriyā hi dharmasya sadaiva śobhanā; yadā naro mṛtyumukhe 'bhivartate
english: No fixed time for dharma is appointed to a man, nor does death await a man's leisure; the practice of dharma is at all times fair — for a man stands ever within the very mouth of death.

sanskrit: yathāndhaḥ svagṛhe yukto hy abhyāsād eva gacchati tathā yuktena manasā prājño gacchati tāṃ gatim
english: As a blind man, well-acquainted with his own house, goes about by mere practice, so, with a mind made steadfast, the wise man goes to that goal.

sanskrit: maraṇaṃ janmani proktaṃ janma vai maraṇāśritam avidvān mokṣadharmeṣu baddho bhramati cakravat
english: Death is declared to lie within birth, and birth indeed rests upon death; the man unlearned in the laws of release, being bound, wanders round and round like a wheel.

sanskrit: yathā mṛṇālo 'nugatam āśu muñcati kardamam tathātmā puruṣasyeha manasā parimucyate manaḥ praṇayate ''tmānaṃ sa enam abhiyuñjati
english: As the lotus-stalk swiftly sheds the mire that clung to it, so the self of a man is here released by the mind; the mind leads the self onward, and it yokes the self to that course.

sanskrit: parārthe vartamānas tu svakāryaṃ yo 'bhimanyate indriyārtheṣu saktaḥ san svakāryāt parihīyate
english: But he who, while toiling for another's ends, fancies it to be his own true task — clinging to the objects of the senses, he falls away from his own true task.

sanskrit: adhas tiryaggatiṃ caiva svarge caiva parāṃ gatim prāpnoti svakṛtair ātmā prājñasyehetarasya ca
english: A downward course, a course athwart, or else the supreme course in heaven — the self attains by its own deeds, whether the man be wise here or otherwise.

sanskrit: mṛnmaye bhājane pakve yathā vai nyasyate dravaḥ tathā śarīraṃ tapasā taptaṃ viṣayam aśnute
english: As liquid is poured into a vessel of clay that has been fired, so the body, tempered by austerity, comes to enjoy its object.

sanskrit: viṣayān aśnute yas tu na sa bhokṣyaty asaṃśayam yas tu bhogāṃs tyajed ātmā sa vai bhoktuṃ vyavasyati
english: He who devours the objects of sense shall, without doubt, not truly enjoy; but the self that renounces its enjoyments — that one is resolved upon the true enjoying.

sanskrit: nīhāreṇa hi saṃvītaḥ śiśnodaraparāyaṇaḥ jātyandha iva panthānam āvṛtātmā na budhyate
english: Wrapped about as if in fog, given over to the cravings of sex and belly, his self veiled, he does not perceive the path, like one blind from birth.

sanskrit: vaṇig yathā samudrād vai yathārthaṃ labhate dhanam tathā martyārṇave jantoḥ karmavijñānato gatiḥ
english: As a merchant gains wealth from the sea according to his purpose, so, upon the ocean of mortal existence, a creature's course follows from the knowledge of its deeds.

sanskrit: ahorātramaye loke jarārūpeṇa saṃcaran mṛtyur grasati bhūtāni pavanaṃ pannago yathā
english: Roaming through this world made of day and night, in the form of old age, Death devours living beings, as the serpent swallows the wind.

sanskrit: svayaṃ kṛtāni karmāṇi jāto jantuḥ prapadyate nākṛtaṃ labhate kaś cit kiṃ cid atra priyāpriyam
english: The deeds it has itself done, the creature, once born, comes to meet; no one here obtains anything, pleasant or unpleasant, that was not first done by him.

sanskrit: śayānaṃ yāntam āsīnaṃ pravṛttaṃ viṣayeṣu ca śubhāśubhāni karmāṇi prapadyante naraṃ sadā
english: Lying down, going forth, seated, or set upon the objects of sense — deeds good and evil come to meet a man at all times.

sanskrit: na hy anyat tīram āsādya punas tartuṃ vyavasyati durlabho dṛśyate hy asya vinipāto mahārṇave
english: For having reached the farther shore, one does not resolve to cross back again; rare indeed is seen any falling of his into the great ocean once more.

sanskrit: yathā bhārāvasaktā hi naur mahāmbhasi tantunā tathā mano 'bhiyogād vai śarīraṃ pratikarṣati
english: As a laden boat upon the great waters is held by its cable, so the mind, by its exertion, draws the body back toward itself.

sanskrit: yathā samudram abhitaḥ saṃsyūtāḥ sarito 'parāḥ tathādyā prakṛtir yogād abhisaṃsyūyate sadā
english: As, on every side, the several rivers are sewn fast unto the sea, so the primal nature is, by yoga, ever sewn fast and made one.

sanskrit: snehapāśair bahuvidhair āsaktamanaso narāḥ prakṛtisthā viṣīdanti jale saikataveśmavat
english: Men whose minds are caught by the manifold cords of affection, abiding within nature, sink down in despair, like a house of sand within the water.

sanskrit: śarīragṛhasaṃsthasya śaucatīrthasya dehinaḥ buddhimārgaprayātasya sukhaṃ tv iha paratra ca
english: For the embodied one who dwells within the house of the body, whose holy ford is purity, and who has set forth upon the path of wisdom — there is happiness, both here and in the world beyond.
